headline: Google Breaks Ground on Visakhapatnam Hub
deck: Google has broken ground on a $15 billion, gigawatt-scale AI hub. Clearances cover Tarluvada and Rambilli while a third campus faces a wildlife-boundary challenge, and the cooling-water budget remains unpublished.
body: Google has officially broken ground on its landmark AI hub in Visakhapatnam [E1]. The company presents the project as a gigawatt-scale ecosystem [E1]. Planned investment reaches $15 billion over the period from 2026 to 2030 [E1]. The announcement converts abstract cloud capacity into a concrete industrial plan.

State environmental clearances now apply to the Tarluvada and Rambilli campuses [E2]. SEIAA has granted environmental clearance for those two sites [E2]. Total land allotment under the permitted footprint stands at 601.4 acres [E2]. The Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Department appears in the record as a water source for at least one cleared location [E2].

The Human Rights Forum has lodged a separate objection focused on Adavivaram [E3]. HRF contends that the project has not obtained environmental clearance for that campus [E3]. Its reading of the project management plan places the Adavivaram site 0.86 kilometres from the boundary of Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary [E3]. The same plan records a distance of 0.45 kilometres to the eco-sensitive zone [E3].

Those records keep the campuses distinct. Tarluvada and Rambilli carry state environmental clearances [E2]. Adavivaram remains the subject of HRF’s legal and environmental contention instead of an adjudicated finding [E3]. No document in the verified record gives one clearance status to all three parcels [E2][E3].

Water sourcing shows the same incomplete ledger. The public record names Rural Water Supply and Sanitation for at least one permitted site [E2]. It does not publish a complete cooling-water budget for the gigawatt-scale build [E1][E2]. That absence leaves the project’s future draw unquantified in the available documents.

A boring null still holds. The clearances and objection do not demonstrate that the hub has produced a city-wide shortage or caused injury inside the sanctuary boundary [E2][E3]. Google has begun construction, while the disputed operating effects remain prospective [E1]. The record supports a disclosure problem before it supports a finding of environmental harm.

Google’s foundations now occupy surveyed ground once described only as cloud [E1]. Three campuses sit inside different permission records, with measured wildlife distances and an identified water bureaucracy [E2][E3]. Regulators have supplied acreage and boundaries while leaving the full heat-rejection demand outside public view [E1][E2]. Compute has acquired a place on the map before its complete resource ledger has reached the page.
